investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler. The scheduler message is consistent across all three checks: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable scheduling targets and preventing any VM from being allocated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no VM slot is available and preemption cannot free one (no lower-priority victims exist on those 2 nodes), every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This prevents the eval runner from ever reaching the agent-creation API call, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is produced and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority pods are present on those nodes.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes may have lost a required label or taint that previously made them eligible for remote-agent pods, effectively shrinking the schedulable pool from 6 to 2 nodes and making exhaustion more likely.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: a prior eval run or user session may have failed to clean up allocated VMs, consuming the finite resource pool without releasing it.
Quaternary — cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have been provisioned with a resource limit that is too small for concurrent eval and production workloads.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler. The scheduler message is consistent across all three checks: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable scheduling targets and preventing any VM from being allocated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no VM slot is available and preemption cannot free one (no lower-priority victims exist on those 2 nodes), every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This prevents the eval runner from ever reaching the agent-creation API call, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is produced and the expected-output contract is entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority pods are present on those nodes.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes may have lost a required label or taint that previously made them eligible for remote-agent pods, effectively shrinking the schedulable pool from 6 to 2 nodes and making exhaustion more likely.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: a prior eval run or user session may have failed to clean up allocated VMs, consuming the finite resource pool without releasing it.
Quaternary — cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have been provisioned with a resource limit that is too small for concurrent eval and production workloads.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Insufficient Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: 0/6 nodes are available due to insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on 2 nodes and node affinity/selector mismatches on the remaining 4. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the runtime response stage, so zero evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector requirements. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod request is rejected as Unschedulable. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the probe's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never completes, so no runtime response evidence is produced and the contract validation fails with all 5 required fields missing.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes — all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary: Node affinity or node selector configuration on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only 2 of the 6 available nodes, reducing the effective scheduling surface to the 2 already-saturated kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes. The other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible.

Tertiary: A concurrent spike in remote-agent provisioning requests (from users or other eval runs) may have consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the eligible nodes just before or during this eval window, causing transient exhaustion rather than a permanent capacity shortfall.

Lower confidence: The node affinity/selector rules may be overly restrictive, excluding nodes that could otherwise host kata peer-pod workloads if the selector were broadened or if additional nodes were labeled appropriately.

If sibling checks for other features (non-remote-agents) also failed at the same time with unrelated errors, a broader cluster or API-plane issue may be the true root cause rather than kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion specifically.

If the local-agent-runtime or local-agent-create checks passed during the same run window, that would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote (kata peer-pod) scheduling path and not a general agent provisioning or API failure.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity directly (e.g., verifying allocatable > 0 on at least one eligible node) before attempting agent creation, so capacity exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct, early-failing check rather than a timeout buried in the agent-create flow.

Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms remote-agent pods created by eval probes are terminated within a bounded window, catching cleanup failures that could contribute to resource exhaustion.

Consider a canary eval that runs remote-agent-create with a short timeout and reports a warning (rather than fail) when scheduling latency exceeds a lower threshold (e.g., 30s), providing earlier signal before full exhaustion occurs.
